lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.focus: graphing half-planes as inequality solution sets
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: graphing half-planes as inequality solution sets

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: How many solutions has 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 11?

steps: The lines are parallel and distinct.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Is the point (2, 3) in the solution region of -2x − 4y ≤ 1?
choices: Yes; substituting gives -16 ≤ 1.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
No; substituting gives -16, which is greater than 1.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 2 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system is equivalent only when 2 is 1.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  2x − 6y = 7
  3x − 6y = 10
choices: infinitely many solutions
exactly two solutions
no solution
exactly one solution

items.prompt: Is the point (-5, -8) in the solution region of 2x − 5y ≤ 10?
choices: Yes; substituting gives 30 ≤ 10.
No; substituting gives 30, which is greater than 10.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 5 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system is equivalent only when 5 is 1.

choices: No; substituting gives -38, which is greater than 4.
